threats.description: A legitimate and well-recorded decision proceeds without access to materially relevant situated knowledge.
The authority controlling the proposed effect also controls the channels used to certify epistemic adequacy.
A complete decision receipt is incorrectly treated as proof that all relevant knowledge was discoverable.

transitions.trigger: material knowledge-path gap or qualifying objection
validity period elapsed or material conditions changed

notes: Epistemic adequacy is a bounded assurance conclusion, not a guarantee of complete knowledge or correct outcome.
Authority, delegation, enforcement, expiry, override, and redress remain explicit.
